title: What Comes After Harm? Mapping Reparative Actions in AI Through Justice Frameworks

live_model.evidence: "We used GPT-4 Turbo, accessed via the OpenAI API, to assist with this multi-label classification task" (coding 1,060 AIAAIC incidents against a reparative-action taxonomy); validated against 200 human-annotated incidents, "the LLM achieved 87% accuracy on actions and 79% on stakeholders"

prompt.location: Appendix C (example of the final prompt), Appendix D (summary statistics and prompt details)
prompt.note: Two-step prompting pipeline: extract stakeholder-action pairs, then classify presence/absence of each taxonomy category.

claim.metric: none for the paper's own contribution (the taxonomy/mapping of reparative actions); the 87%/79% validation accuracy is an internal QA check on the coding tool, not the paper's benchmarked subject
claim.location: Sec. "Analyzing Reparative Actions At Scale" (validation on 200 incidents, 20 per action category)

data.source: AIAAIC incident database (1,060 incidents; public repository of AI harm reports)

notes: AIES 2025. GPT-4 Turbo is an auxiliary qualitative-coding tool used to scale up the authors' own taxonomy across a harms database, not the paper's object of study, matching the role-A pattern used elsewhere in this batch (e.g. W4412886885, W4416034827) despite a clean validation accuracy being available.
